stereotypeDefinition.comment: One row of a File Classification's `Entries` list: which files (Glob), how important it is to review changes to them (Review Importance), and what they are (Classification). Exists only as an `Entries` row; it is never applied to an element directly.
stereotypeDefinition.name: File Classification Entry

property.hint: Which files this row applies to, as .gitignore-style patterns, one per line, e.g. `**/*.cs` or `Payments/**/*`. Paths are relative to the element the stereotype is on: the application's output location for the root folder, a folder or project's directory, each contained project's root for a solution folder, or the folder containing a Template Output. A line starting with `!` excludes, and within one row the last matching line wins. Leave empty to match every file.
property.name: Glob

property.hint: How important it is for a reviewer to look at changes to the matched files: `3 - High` for changes that need careful review (e.g. security, payments, personal data), down to `0 - None` for files whose changes need no special attention. Set the full option text, e.g. `2 - Medium`.
property.name: Review Importance

property.hint: One or more `File Classification` elements describing what the matched files are, e.g. "Data Access" or "PCI scope". These are the named categories under the root folder's `File Classifications` element (a different thing from this stereotype, despite the shared name). Create one there first if none fits.
property.name: Classification
